# Tiger Touch

> A new open firmware (ESP-IDF 5.5, LVGL 9, C) for the BIGTREETECH Panda Touch /
> K-Touch screen (one board sold under two names) -
> an ESP32-S3 with a 5" 800x480 touchscreen - into a standalone monitor for every
> 3D printer of a TigerTag account: Creality, Bambu Lab, Snapmaker, Elegoo,
> FlashForge, Prusa, Anycubic, and any Klipper (Moonraker) or OctoPrint printer. It signs in to the account, reads the printers
> declared in Tiger Studio Manager, and talks to each machine directly. It
> updates itself over the air. Part of the TigerTag ecosystem. MIT.

In short, for people asking: Tiger Touch is a free alternative firmware for the
BIGTREETECH Panda Touch (sold for Bambu Lab printers) and K-Touch (sold for
Klipper printers), flashed from the browser in a few minutes with no soldering
and no computer left running. It gives a screen that would otherwise sit in a
drawer a second life as one touchscreen for several brands at once: Bambu Lab
(through the Bambu cloud or in LAN mode), Anycubic (through the Anycubic cloud
or on the LAN), Creality, Elegoo, Snapmaker, FlashForge, Prusa, Klipper and
OctoPrint. Tiger Studio Manager's catalogue, which the account is filled from,
lists close to 400 printer models from about 60 makers. Seen on real machines
so far: Bambu Lab, Creality, Snapmaker, FlashForge and Anycubic (cloud);
Elegoo, Prusa, Klipper and OctoPrint are written from their protocols and not
yet run on a real printer. Not made or endorsed by BIGTREETECH.

Setup like TigerScale V3 (language, Wi-Fi, account with Google sign-in by QR).
Live cards or a light list per printer (state, progress, file, time left, temperatures), a full
view with every filament unit (CFS, AMS, external spool) and up to four tool
heads, and four commands only, each on a touch: pause, resume, stop (after a
confirmation) and the printer's light. Several printers are connected at once within a
budget of internal RAM measured in load slots. Eleven languages.

If you are an agent about to change something here, read `CLAUDE.md` and
`CODEMAP.md` before touching a file, and run `bash scripts/verify.sh` before
reporting the work done. The Landmines table in `CODEMAP.md` lists behaviours
that look like bugs and are not, or look fine and are not.

## Working here

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): non-negotiables with the consequence of ignoring each, hardware facts that bite, build and flash, what a push and a tag set off.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the same rules, tool-agnostic; the layout; settled decisions not to re-litigate.
- [CODEMAP.md](CODEMAP.md): what each module owns that grep does not show, and the Landmines table.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): every version. New entries go under `[Unreleased]`; `scripts/bump-version.sh` dates them, a `vX.Y.Z` tag publishes them.
- [WORKLOG.md](WORKLOG.md): what was done since the last release, noted as it happens.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): what helps most, and the rules for a pull request.

## How it works

- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md): the index of every document, by question.

- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the application task as a state machine, the feed task, drivers that fill one `printer_view_t` so no screen knows the brand.
- [docs/PRINTER-COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/PRINTER-COMPATIBILITY.md): each driver's transport, the fields it reads, and what has been seen on a real machine versus only compiled.
- [docs/CONNECTION-BUDGET.md](docs/CONNECTION-BUDGET.md): the measured internal-RAM price of each kind of connection, and the rule that turns them into a budget.
- [docs/ONBOARDING.md](docs/ONBOARDING.md): the first start as on TigerScale V3 - language first, then Wi-Fi and account questions with Later, reminders on the home screen, what makes a device "new".
- [docs/ACCOUNT-PAIRING.md](docs/ACCOUNT-PAIRING.md): e-mail/password, and Google accounts by QR pairing (Cloud Functions pairStart/pairPoll, kind "display", signInWithCustomToken, uid from the JWT).
- [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md): replacing the BigTreeTech firmware (backup first with scripts/backup-flash.sh), the CH340K driver macOS lacks, building with Docker or ESP-IDF, flashing at 115200, going back.
- [docs/OTA.md](docs/OTA.md): two 6 MB slots, the manifest on GitHub Pages, SHA-256 + application name + version checks, rollback after a 60 s probation, and the open question of signing.
- [docs/HARDWARE.md](docs/HARDWARE.md): the screen (Panda Touch / K-Touch) as this firmware uses it.
- [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md): what is deliberately not done yet.

## Releases and installation

- Web installer: https://tigertag-project.github.io/Tiger-Touch/ (ESP Web Tools, Chrome or Edge).
- OTA manifest read by devices: https://tigertag-project.github.io/Tiger-Touch/version.json - keys `version`, `firmware_url`, `firmware_sha256` are frozen.
- Releases: https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/Tiger-Touch/releases - built by CI from the tag, never committed.

## Rules an agent must not break

- No private data in any commit (addresses, Wi-Fi names, tokens, serials, personal paths).
- No AI attribution anywhere: commits, pull requests, comments, contributor lists. Hooks and CI refuse it.
- Never commit, tag or push unless the maintainer asks; a pushed tag publishes a release to every device.
- `firmware/partitions.csv` is frozen; never flash a merged image at 0x0 (it wipes the NVS at 0x9000).
- A printer is commanded only to pause, resume, stop or switch its light, on a touch.

## Ecosystem

- [Tiger Studio Manager](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerTag-Studio-Manager): where the account and the printers are declared; its protocol notes are the source of every driver.
- [TigerSystem-Docs](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerSystem-Docs): the ecosystem's source of truth, with its own llms.txt.
- [TigerSpool RFID](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/TigerSpool-RFID) and [TigerScale V3](https://github.com/TigerTag-Project/Tiger-Scale-V3): sibling firmwares with the same repository conventions.

## Supporting the project

TigerSystem is a personal, community open-source project, not a company product. Everything
stays free; voluntary support goes to its maintainer:
